(a) professors, lecturers of any class or persons engaged in research; or
(b) holders of posts declared by the Senate to be academic posts;

3 Establishment of University
(1) There is hereby constituted a university to be known as the Midlands State University.
[inserted by the General Laws Amendment (No.2) Act 2002 promulgated on the 24th January, 2003 - with retrospective
effect, in terms of clause 47 - from the 4th February, 2002
(2) The University shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and shall be capable of suing and being sued
in its corporate name and, subject to this Act, of performing all acts that bodies corporate may by law perform

[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 13]
4 Objects and powers of the University
(1) The objects of the University are the advancement of knowledge, the diffusion and extension of arts, science and
learning, the preservation, dissemination and enhancement of knowledge that is relevant for the development of the
people of Zimbabwe through teaching and learning, research, community service, innovation and industrialisation and, so
far as is consistent with those objects, the nurturing of the intellectual, aesthetic, social and moral growth of the students
at the University.
[Subsection (1) substituted by Act 4/2022 w.e.f. 2nd September, 2022.]
(2) For the achievement of its objects, the University shall, subject to this Act, have the following powers-

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 13]
(2) For the achievement of its objects, the University shall, subject to this Act, have the following powers-
(a) to provide for research and courses of instruction, whether on a full-time or part-time basis by
correspondence or extra-murally, and to take such other steps as may appear necessary and desirable for
the advancement and dissemination of knowledge;
(b) to hold examinations and to confer degrees, including honorary degrees, diplomas, certificates and other
awards, upon persons who have followed a course or courses of study approved by the Senate and
additionally, or alternatively, have satisfied such other requirements as may be determined by the
Senate;
(c) to provide courses not leading to degrees, diplomas or certificates, including training for persons wishing

5 Membership of the University
The University shall consist of-
(a) a Chancellor; and
(b) a Vice-Chancellor; and
(c) 1 or more Pro-Vice-Chancellors; and
(d) members of the Council; and
(e) members of the Senate; and
(f) members of staff; and

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 15]
[amended by the General Laws Amendment (No.2) Act 2002 promulgated on the 24th January, 2003 - with retrospective
effect, in terms of clause 47 - from the 4th February, 2002
(g) registered students; and
(h) the Convocation.

6 Prohibition against discrimination in membership of University
(1) No test of religious or political belief, race, ethnic origin, nationality or gender shall be imposed upon or required
of any person in order to entitle him to be admitted as a member of staff or student of the University or to hold any office
therein or privilege thereof.
(2) Nothing in subsection (1) shall be construed as preventing the University from giving preference to citizens or
residents of Zimbabwe when making appointments or promotions or when admitting students.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 15]
7 Chancellor
(1) The President of Zimbabwe shall be Chancellor of the University.
(2) The Chancellor shall be the head of the University.
(3) The Chancellor shall have the right-
(a) to preside over any assembly or meeting held by or under the authority of the University; and
(b) upon the recommendation of the Council and the Senate, to confer degrees, diplomas, certificates and
other awards and distinctions of the University and to withdraw or restore such awards.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 15]
8 Vice-Chancellor
(1) The Vice-Chancellor shall be appointed by the Chancellor after consultation with the Minister and the Council
and shall hold office for such period as is provided in his contract of employment.
(2) Subject to the general control of the Council, the Vice-Chancellor shall be the chief academic, administrative and
disciplinary officer of the University, with general responsibility for maintaining and promoting the efficiency,
effectiveness and good order of the University.
(3) Subject to subsections (4) and (5), the Vice-Chancellor may-
(a) suspend from duty any member of staff of the University;
(b) subject to section six, prohibit the admission of a student or any person to the University;

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 16]
(i) a member of staff, which is recommended by the Staff Disciplinary Committee in terms
of subsection (6) of section twenty-six;
(ii) a student, which is recommended by the Student Disciplinary Committee in terms of subsection
(6) of section twenty-seven.
(4) The Vice-Chancellor shall not expel a student for misconduct unless the student has been found guilty of
misconduct by the Student Disciplinary Committee in terms of section twenty-seven.
(5) Any action taken by the Vice-Chancellor in terms of subsection (3) shall be subject to ratification by the Council.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 16]
9 Pro-Vice-Chancellors
(1) 1 or more Pro-Vice-Chancellors may be appointed by the Council with the approval of the Minister and in
accordance with the Statutes.
(2) A Pro-Vice-Chancellor shall assist the Vice-Chancellor in the performance of his functions and, in addition, shall
have such functions as may be specified in the Statutes.
(3) The Vice-Chancellor may delegate to a Pro-Vice-Chancellor, either absolutely or subject to conditions, any of his
functions in terms of this Act and may at any time amend or withdraw any such delegation:
Provided that the delegation of a function in terms of this subsection shall not prevent the Vice-
Chancellor from himself exercising that function.

text:

10 Council
[Substituted by Act 4/2022 w.e.f. 2nd September, 2022.]
(1) Subject to this Act and any general directions as to policy given by the Minister, the government and executive
authority of the University shall be vested in the Council which shall consist of not less than ten (10) and not more than
twenty (20) members including-
(a) the Chancellor and the Vice-Chancellor (and the Pro-Vice Chancellors who may attend the Council
meeting at the invitation of the Vice Chancellor but shall not have voting privileges), who shall be ex-
officio members; and
(b) 10 persons appointed by the Minister including a Ministry representative; and
(c) 2 persons who are members of the academic staff appointed by the Senate, other than the Vice-
Chancellor and any Pro-Vice-Chancellor; and

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 16]
(c) 2 persons who are members of the academic staff appointed by the Senate, other than the Vice-
Chancellor and any Pro-Vice-Chancellor; and
(d) the President of the Students' Representative Council, who shall be an ex-officio member; and
(e) 2 persons elected by the workers' committee of the University.
(2) In appointing members to the Council, the Minister or any appointing authority under this section shall-
(a) ensure that both genders are equally represented and for the avoidance of doubt that women constitute
half the membership of the Council; and
(b) ensure that there is fair regional representation;
(c) appoint members of relevant and appropriate professions.

text:

11 Functions of Council
(1) Subject to this Act and the Statutes, the Council shall-
(a) appoint, with the approval of the Minister, the Pro-Vice Chancellors and the Registrar; and
(b) appoint the Bursar, the Librarian, the academic staff, the administrative staff and other employees of the
University:
Provided that the Council may delegate its duties under this paragraph to such committee as may be
prescribed in the Statutes;
(c) on the recommendation of the Senate, institute professorships, associate professorships and other
academic offices, and abolish or hold in abeyance any such offices;
(d) receive and, if the Council considers it proper to do so, give effect to reports and recommendations from

12 Disqualifications for appointment as a Council member
The Minister shall not appoint a person as a member of Council and no person shall be qualified to hold office as a
member of Council who-
(a) is not a citizen of Zimbabwe or permanently resident in Zimbabwe; or
(b) has in terms of any law in force in any country-
(i) been adjudged or otherwise declared insolvent or bankrupt and has not been rehabilitated or
discharged; or
(ii) made an assignment to, or arrangement or composition with, his creditors which has not been
rescinded or set aside; or
(c) has, within the period of 5 years immediately preceding the date of his proposed appointment, been
sentenced in any country to a term of imprisonment of or exceeding 6 months, whether or not any

sentenced in any country to a term of imprisonment of or exceeding 6 months, whether or not any
portion has been suspended, imposed without the option of a fine and has not received a free pardon.
13 Vacation of office by Council member
A member shall vacate office and his office shall become vacant-
(a) after giving the Minister such period of notice of his intention to resign as may be fixed in his conditions
of appointment or, if no such period has been fixed, after the expiry of 1 month or of such other period
of notice as he and the Minister may agree; or
(b) on the date he begins to serve a sentence of imprisonment, the term which is not less than 6 months,
whether or not any portion has been suspended, imposed without the option of a fine in any country; or

effect, in terms of clause 47 - from the 4th February, 2002

14 Chairman and vice-chairman of Council
(1) The Council shall elect a chairman and a vice-chairman from amongst its members to hold office for such period

(2) At all meetings of the Council at which the Chancellor is not present the chairman of the Council or, in his
absence, the vice-chairman shall preside.
(3) If at any meeting of the Council the Chancellor and the chairman and vice-chairman of the Council are all absent,
the members of the Council who are present shall elect a person from amongst their number to preside at the meeting.

(a) any person so employed shall be entitled to resign from his employment on giving such notice in writing
to the Registrar as may be fixed in such terms and conditions;

Council, whose decision shall be final.

No decision or act of the Council, the Senate, the Convocation or any board or committee established by or in terms

(a) the Council, Senate, Convocation, board or committee, as the case may be, consisted of fewer than the

writing addressed to the Minister.
[Amended by Act 4/2022 w.e.f. 2nd September, 2022.]
Casual vacancies in Council
3. Any casual vacancy occurring among the appointed or elected members of the Council shall be filled as soon as possible

text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 29]
Casual vacancies in Council
3. Any casual vacancy occurring among the appointed or elected members of the Council shall be filled as soon as possible
by the person, persons or body which appointed or elected the member whose place has become vacant, and the person so
appointed or elected shall hold office for the remainder of the period for which the person whose place he fills was
appointed or elected.
Meetings and quorum of Council
4. (1) The Council shall meet at least 3 times a year.
(2) The quorum of the Council shall be one-half of the members holding office at the time of the meeting.
Resolutions by circulation among members of Council
5. A resolution proposed by the Executive Committee of the Council, other than for the purpose of making a Statute, which

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 29]
5. A resolution proposed by the Executive Committee of the Council, other than for the purpose of making a Statute, which
is on its authority circulated by the Registrar to all members of the Council and which receives the written agreement of
not less than two-thirds of such members shall, upon receipt of such agreement by the Registrar, have the same force and
effect as a resolution passed at a meeting of the Council.
Chairman and Vice-Chairman of Council
5A. (1) The Council shall elect from among its members a Chairman and a Vice-Chairman, each to hold office for a
period not exceeding three years, and each of whom shall be eligible for re-election.
(2) If both the Chairman and the Vice-Chairman are absent from a meeting of the Council the members present shall

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 29]
(2) If both the Chairman and the Vice-Chairman are absent from a meeting of the Council the members present shall
appoint from among themselves a chairman for the purpose of that meeting.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 30]
(3) If both the Chairman and the Vice-Chairman are at the same time unable to carry out their duties the Council may
elect one of its members to perform such duties during such time.

effect, in terms of clause 47 - from the 4th February, 2002
Meetings and quorum of Senate
6. (1) The Senate shall meet at least three times a year.
(2) The quorum of the Senate shall be one-half of the members holding office at the time of the meeting.
(3) The Vice-Chancellor or, in his absence, a Pro-Vice-Chancellor, shall be chairman of the Senate.
Convocation
7. There shall be no quorum for meetings of the Convocation, the proceedings of which shall be regulated by the chairman

text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 30]
Convocation
7. There shall be no quorum for meetings of the Convocation, the proceedings of which shall be regulated by the chairman
subject to any general or special direction of the Council.
Faculties
8. The University shall include such faculties as may from time to time be established by the Council.
Deans
9. (1) There shall be a dean of each faculty, who shall be appointed by a selection board appointed by the Council and
chaired by the Vice-Chancellor or a Pro-Vice-Chancellor.
(2) A dean shall hold office for 3 years and, on the expiry of his term of office, shall be eligible for re-appointment,
subject to statute 12.
Functions of deans
10. (1) A dean shall be responsible to the Vice-Chancellor for-
(a) the character and quality of his faculty's academic programmes and teaching; and

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 30]
10. (1) A dean shall be responsible to the Vice-Chancellor for-
(a) the character and quality of his faculty's academic programmes and teaching; and
(b) the proper direction, control and management of the staff, property, equipment and finances of his
faculty; and
(c) contributing to the evolution and maintenance of an environment conducive to learning at the University.
(2) Without limiting subsection (1), a dean's functions include-
(a) the planning and control of his faculty's budget; and
(b) implementing the policies and objectives of the University and his faculty; and
(c) developing and maintaining relations with alumni of his faculty and with other organizations and
persons, with a view to enriching the academic programmes offered by his faculty; and

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 31]
(d) soliciting funds and other assistance to support programmes and projects of his faculty; and
(e) co-operating with other faculties, agencies and entities to further the programmes and projects of his
faculty; and
(f) performing such other functions as may be prescribed by Ordinance.
Evaluation of performance of dean
11. The performance of every dean shall be evaluated annually by a committee appointed by the Vice-Chancellor and
consisting of senior academic staff and administrative staff.
Termination of appointment of dean
12. (1) A dean may resign his office as such by giving the Vice-Chancellor one month's written notice or such longer or
shorter notice as he and the Vice-Chancellor may agree.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 31]
shorter notice as he and the Vice-Chancellor may agree.
(2) Subject to the approval of the Council, the Vice-Chancellor may suspend or terminate the appointment of a person
as dean-
(a) on the recommendation of a committee referred to in section 11; or
(b) for other good cause.
(3) A Dean whose appointment has been suspended or terminated in terms of subsection (2) may appeal to the
Council within fourteen days of being notified of the suspension or termination, and on any such appeal the Council may
confirm, vary or rescind the suspension or termination, as the case may be, or give such other direction in the matter as it
thinks appropriate.
Composition of faculty boards
13. For each faculty there shall be a faculty board which shall consist of-

thinks appropriate.
Composition of faculty boards
13. For each faculty there shall be a faculty board which shall consist of-
(a) all the full-time academic staff of the faculty; and
(b) such persons as may be assigned to the faculty board by the Senate; and
(c) two students elected annually by the students in the faculty.
Functions of faculty boards
14. A faculty board shall have the following functions-
(a) to regulate, subject to the approval of the Senate, the teaching and study of the subjects assigned to the
faculty;
(b) to report to the Senate on any matter specifically relating to the work of the faculty;
(c) to deal with any matter referred or delegated to it by the Senate;

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 32]
(d) to appoint committees, which may include a minority of persons who are not members of the faculty
board, to carry out any of the duties or exercise any of the powers of the board.
Meetings of faculty boards
15. (1) The dean of each faculty shall call regular meetings of the faculty board at which matters relating to the policy of
the faculty and appointments shall be discussed and recommendations adopted for submission to the appropriate
authorities on appointments.
(2) The Vice-Chancellor and every Pro-Vice-Chancellor shall be entitled to attend any meeting of a faculty board or
any committee thereof.
Teaching Departments
16. (1) The teaching departments and their allocation to faculties shall be prescribed by ordinance.

any committee thereof.
Teaching Departments
16. (1) The teaching departments and their allocation to faculties shall be prescribed by ordinance.
(2) A chairman of department shall be appointed by the Vice-Chancellor, on behalf of the Council, from among, the
full-time members of the academic staff of the department, after consultation with each member of the academic staff in
the department and the dean of the faculty to which the department is allocated.
(3) A chairman of department shall hold office for a period of 3 years, or such other period as may be determined by
ordinance, and shall be eligible for re-appointment.
(4) A department may be allocated to two or more faculties.

ordinance, and shall be eligible for re-appointment.
(4) A department may be allocated to two or more faculties.
Institutes and centres
17. The Council, after consultation with the Senate, may establish institutes or centres of learning within or outside the
University and shall appoint the head of any such institute or centre and give directions as to its studies and research and
administration.
Appointment of Registrar, Bursar and Librarian
18. (1) For the purpose of considering appointments to the offices of Registrar, Bursar and Librarian, there shall be a
joint committee of the Council and the Senate consisting of-
(a) the chairman of the Council, who shall be the chairman of the joint committee; and
(b) the vice-chairman of the Council; and
(c) the Vice-Chancellor; and

text:

(b) the vice-chairman of the Council; and
(c) the Vice-Chancellor; and
(d) every Pro-Vice-Chancellor; and
(e) two persons appointed by the Council from among its members who are not members of the Senate; and
(f) three persons appointed by the Senate from among its members.
(2) The joint committee constituted by this Statute shall consider each applicant to a vacancy in the office of
Registrar, Bursar or Librarian and shall make recommendations thereon to the Council.

Procedure generally
19. (1) Except as otherwise specifically provided by the Act or, these Statutes, in the absence of the chairman or vice-
chairman at a meeting of a board or committee the members present shall elect from those present a chairman to preside
over that meeting.
(2) Except as otherwise specifically provided by the Act or these Statutes, the quorum at any meeting of a board or
committee shall be as fixed by the person or authority that appointed the board or committee.
(3) Except as otherwise specifically provided by the Act or these Statutes, each board or committee shall determine
and may make rules for the time, place and procedure of its meetings.
(4) The minutes of a meeting of a board or committee shall be laid on the table at the next following meeting of the

(4) The minutes of a meeting of a board or committee shall be laid on the table at the next following meeting of the
body that appointed it.
(5) At a meeting of board or committee, in the event of an equality of votes on any matter, the person presiding shall
have a casting vote in addition to his deliberative vote.
(6) Subsections (3), (4) and (5) shall apply, mutatis mutandis, to the Council and the Senate, save that minutes of the
Council shall be sent to the Chancellor and the Minister and a report of each meeting of the Council shall be laid on the
table at a meeting of the Council.
Financial procedures
20. (1) The Council shall fix the financial year of the University.

Financial procedures
20. (1) The Council shall fix the financial year of the University.
(2) The Finance Committee shall submit to the Council, before the beginning of the financial year, draft estimates of
income and expenditure, and such estimates, amended as the Council thinks fit, shall be approved by the Council before
the beginning of the financial year.
(3) The Council may revise the estimates during the course of the financial year and give directions for the manner in
which amendments of expenditure estimates may be made, which directions may make provision for delegating the
powers of revision so long as such delegation does not extend to altering the total estimated expenditure.

powers of revision so long as such delegation does not extend to altering the total estimated expenditure.
(4) As soon as practicable after the end of the financial year, a balance sheet and income and expenditure account
with supporting schedules shall be submitted to the auditors.
(5) The audited accounts, with any comments thereon made by the auditors, shall be submitted to the Council.

21. (1) Subject to subsections (2) and (3), the Council shall, before the beginning of each financial year, appoint as
auditors persons who are registered as public auditors in terms of the Public Accountants and Auditors Act [Chapter

holds any other office in the University.
(3) If no appointment of new auditors is made before the beginning of any financial year, the auditors in office shall
continue in office.
(4) An auditor appointed in terms of subsection (1) shall be entitled at all reasonable times to require any officer,
employee or agent of the University-

HISTORICAL NOTE

Devolution

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 74]
The idea of a University in the Midlands dates back to the foundation of the National University of Science and
Technology when Gweru, which was identified as a possible site for a second university campus, lost its bid to Bulawayo
and the Province of Matabeleland. Two other opportunities to host institutions of higher learning (the Open University
and the Catholic University) were also missed by the Midlands Province when the two universities went to Harare instead.
It was in the midst of such disappointments that two initiatives gradually converged to give birth to what has since become
the Midlands State University. The then President of the Republic of Zimbabwe, His Excellency, Cde. Robert Gabriel

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 74]
the Midlands State University. The then President of the Republic of Zimbabwe, His Excellency, Cde. Robert Gabriel
Mugabe, on the nudging of the provincial political leadership of the Midlands, acceded to the idea of a national university
being built in the Midlands and announced that at two provincial rallies held at Gokwe and Mataga growth points. The
President's declarations coincided with the Ministry of Higher Education and Technology's policy of devolution, which
was aimed at expanding access to higher education by converting teachers' and technical colleges into degree-granting
institutions. These colleges would offer Bachelor of Education and Bachelor of Technology degree programmes.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 74]
In line with the devolution policy, the then Minister of Higher Education and Technology, the Hon, Dr S.I Mudenge
appointed in October 1995 the Committee on the Devolution of Bachelor of Education and Bachelor of Technology
Degree Programmes, which was chaired by Professor C.J Chetsanga to investigate the feasibility of upgrading teachers'
and technical colleges into degree granting places. The Committee recommended that Gweru Teachers College spearhead
the process, followed by Masvingo and Chinhoyi Teachers' Colleges and that Gweru starts by offering Bachelor of
Education degrees. The next Minister of Higher Education, Hon. Dr I.M.C Chombo set up in June 1996 another committee

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 74]
Education degrees. The next Minister of Higher Education, Hon. Dr I.M.C Chombo set up in June 1996 another committee
chaired by Prof. H.A.M Dzinotyiwei to advise on the details of getting degree programmes going at Gweru Teachers

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 75]
College. The Dzinotyiwei Committee recommended that the college should offer BA-Education, BSc - Education and B.
Com- Education degree programmes under some special relationship with the University of Zimbabwe for four years
before becoming an independent and fully-fledged university. A third committee of professionals chaired by Dr R.J
Zvobgo, the Principal of Gweru Teachers College made the final recommendations on the initial staffing needs and degree
programmes. These recommendations laid the basis on which the first-degree students were enrolled for Bachelor of
Commerce with Education and Bachelor of Science with Education degrees offered by the University of Zimbabwe
through the Faculty of Education's Department of Teacher Education.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 75]
Establishment of the University
In the meantime, although the devolution policy inaugurated an irrevocable process of bringing university education to
the Midlands, there was a strong feeling, especially in the Province, that what was being done did not quite amount to the
President's promise of a fully-fledged state university in the province. Responding to these feelings, but without losing
sight of constraints imposed on the Government by declining national funds, the Minister of Higher Education and
Technology transformed the devolution project at Gweru into Zimbabwe's third state university by means of the State
University in the Midlands Act of April 1999.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 75]
The new University, whose name was later changed to the Midlands State University, was to be initially housed at the
Gweru Teachers College premises. The mandate of the institution was contained in its broad objectives which are the
advancement of knowledge, the diffusion and extension of arts, science and learning, preservation, dissemination and
enhancement of knowledge that is relevant for the development of the people of Zimbabwe through teaching and research
and, so far, as is consistent with the objectives, the nurturing of the intellectual, aesthetic, social and moral growth of the
students at the University.

text:

Zimbabwe, a Council, Vice Chancellor, Pro Vice Chancellors and Senate.
To immediately manage the implementation of the Act, the Government, through the Ministry of Higher Education and
Technology, appointed an inaugural Council with the following 21 members drawn from all walks of life and professions:

text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 75]
Founding Vice-Chancellor and Pro-Vice-Chancellor
In consultation with the then Minister of Higher Education and Technology, Dr I. Chombo, and with the approval of the
then President and Chancellor of the University, His Excellency, Cde R.G Mugabe, the inaugural Council appointed a
distinguished academic and historian, Professor Ngwabi Bhebe, as the first Vice-Chancellor with effect from December
1999 and a renowned educationist, Professor Rungano Zvobgo, as Pro-Vice- Chancellor in January 2000.
Campus Sites
The University was initially granted use of facilities of the former Gweru Teachers College, Batanai Complex in Senga
and the Senga Institute of Manpower Planning and Development. The site originally offered by the City of Gweru had to

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 75]
and the Senga Institute of Manpower Planning and Development. The site originally offered by the City of Gweru had to
be abandoned in deference to the Zimbabwe National Army, who are using it as a training ground. The University was
later granted 164 hectares of State land by the Vungu Rural District Council. This land stretches westwards from the

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 76]
former Gweru Teachers College. In addition, the University later acquired 188.6ha of land from TelOne, where more
facilities were put up to aid in teaching and learning. As of the year 2024, this campus is home to the Graduate School of
Business Leadership, Faculty of Law, Faculty of Education, Faculty of Business Sciences, Midlands State University
National Pathology Research and Diagnostic Centre, Midlands State University National Language Institute and
Innovation Hub under the Research and Innovation Directorate.

As part of its growth strategy, the University adopted a multicampus approach. To date, the University has a presence in
Gweru, Zvishavane, Harare, Kwekwe and Bulawayo.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 76]
In fulfilment of the ten-faculty vision, the University, further, established the following faculties:
1. Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences
2. Faculty of Engineering and Geosciences
3. Faculty of Built Environment, Art and Design

The University also embarked on a rebranding exercise for all its academic programmes to align them to the provisions
of the heritage-based Education 5.0 philosophy. The rebranding exercise has resulted in changes to some faculty names
as well as the introduction of new academic programmes.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 76]
The University's ten faculties and three research institutes are distributed as follows:
Ø
The Gweru Main Campus hosts five faculties, namely; Social Sciences, Science and Technology, Medicine and
Health Sciences, and Agriculture, Environment and Natural Resources Management. In addition, the Gweru campus

• MSU National Pathology Research and Diagnostic Centre
• Gender Institute
• Centre for Public Policy and Devolution

disseminate continuous valid information on the social, economic, political, industrial and environmental impact of
the dam on society.
Ø
Harare Campus situated at number 1, Kwame Nkrumah Avenue is home to the Harare Weekend School that offers

text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 76]
Academic Programmes and Vision of the University
The first task for the Council and its Vice-Chancellor designates was to come up with proposals for academic programmes,
which in turn would provide a basis for drawing up a university budget, staff recruitment and student admissions. It was
also necessary to have a provisional working vision and mission statement for the new institution, which would be refined
and concretized in due course in consultation with all the institutional and national stakeholders.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 77]
Such a vision envisaged a ten-faculty university whose principal mission was to train human resources innovatively and
to generate, through original and applied research, scientific knowledge, which would substantially contribute to the social
and economic development of Zimbabwe. The vision also has in sight a modern university whose delivery methods aim
at breaking down traditional boundaries between vocational training and academic teaching using semesterised modular
systems to allow the student as the major client to participate in the formulation and management of his/ her own
programme; and above all at exposing the student to work-related learning to apply theoretical principles and knowledge
to real work situations.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf

Strategic Plan
The University drew up its foundational long-term strategic plan. The exercise provided an opportunity to bring together
the University community and all the national stakeholders. The Strategic Plan provides a guide and a basis for the
development of the institution in terms of the programmes that must be taught; the physical plant, infrastructure and
equipment that must be provided; projections of staff and student numbers by programmes; and work out a long-term
business plan for the University.

Building on the foundational long-term strategic plan, the University introduced and implemented several other strategic
initiatives to further its goals.

Midlands State University Enterprises
In keeping with the Education 5.0 philosophy, the University has made significant efforts to generate third-stream income
through industrialisation which has resulted in the establishment of the MSU Enterprises Division, with interests in
agriculture, chemical manufacturing, clothing and textile, and press and publications.
Furthermore, the University established a vibrant Midlands State University National Pathology Research and
Diagnostic Centre which was fully funded by the Government of Zimbabwe through the Ministry of Higher and Tertiary
Education, Innovation, Science and Technology Development. The Centre offers pathology consultancy and high

Education, Innovation, Science and Technology Development. The Centre offers pathology consultancy and high
technology-driven clinical services and diagnostic imaging services through innovation, biomedical research and
development.
The University also established a National Language Institute. The Centre offers language services that include editing
and translation of documents, and the provision of Sign Language and Braille facilities. The Centre was fully funded by
the Government of Zimbabwe through the Ministry of Higher and Tertiary Education, Innovation, Science and
Technology Development.
In 2021, the University was licenced for MSU Radio and the station was allocated two frequencies, one in Zvishavane at

In 2021, the University was licenced for MSU Radio and the station was allocated two frequencies, one in Zvishavane at
90.3 FM and another in Gweru at 101.7 FM. MSU Radio manned shifts started on February 18, 2023. At the moment the
station is on air every day of the week from 0600hrs to 2100hrs broadcasting programmes such as; Breakfast Show, Mid-
Morning Show, Lunchtime Listening, Drive Time Show and The After Drive. The year 2024 saw the launch of the Our
Destiny (OD) Stores. Established as a retail shop, OD Stores pursue the Education 5.0 blueprint's agenda to locally
produce and distribute goods & services for the nation.

FACULTY GOVERNANCE ORDINANCE NO. 4

1. Executive Deans

i. There shall be an Executive Dean of each Faculty, who shall be appointed by a selection board appointed
by the Council and chaired by the Vice-Chancellor or a Pro-Vice-Chancellor.

ii. An Executive Dean shall hold office for three years and, on the expiry of his term of office, shall be
eligible for re-appointment.

3. Evaluation of Performance of Executive Deans

The performance of every Executive Dean shall be evaluated by a committee appointed by the Vice-
Chancellor and consisting of senior academic staff and administrators.

i. An Executive Dean may resign his office as such by giving the Vice-Chancellor one month's notice or
such longer or shorter notice as he and the Vice-Chancellor may agree.
ii. Subject to the approval of the Council, the Vice-Chancellor may suspend or terminate the appointment
of a person as an Executive Dean: -
a. on the recommendation of the committee referred to in section11; or;
b. for other good cause.
c. an Executive Dean whose appointment as such has been suspended or terminated in terms of

text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 81]
5. Composition of Faculty Boards

For each Faculty there shall be a Faculty Board which shall consist of:
a. the Executive Dean;
b. all the full-time academic staff of the Faculty; such persons as may be assigned to the Faculty Board by
the Senate; and
c. two students elected annually by the students in the Faculty.

6. Functions of Faculty Boards

A Faculty Board shall have the following functions:
a. to regulate, subject to the approval of the Senate, the teaching and study of the
subjects assigned to the faculty;
b. to report to the Senate on any matter specifically relating to the work of the faculty;

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 82]
c. to deal with any matter referred or delegated to it by the Senate; and
d. to appoint committees, which may include a minority of persons who are not members of the Faculty
Board, to carry out any of the duties or exercise any of the powers of the Board.

7. Meetings of Faculty Boards
i. The Executive Dean of each faculty shall call for at least three (3) meetings of the Faculty Board
at which matters relating to the policy of the faculty and appointments shall be discussed and
recommendations adopted for submission to the appropriate authorities on appointments.
ii. The Vice-Chancellor and every Pro-Vice-Chancellor shall be entitled to attend
any meeting of a Faculty Board or committee thereof.

PREAMBLE

In terms of section 29 (3) (h) of the Midlands State University Act [Chapter 25:21] as amended, the Council of Midlands
State University, with the approval of the Minister of Higher and Tertiary Education, Innovation, Science and Technology
Development, or such other Minister to whom the President may from time to time assign the administration of the Midlands
State University Act on the recommendation of the University Senate, makes the following Ordinance:

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 87]
1. INTERPRETATION
In this Ordinance, 'academic staff'' means all persons employed by the University as Professors/Research Professors,
Associate Professors/Associate Research Professors, Senior Lecturers/Senior Research Fellows, Lecturers/Research
Fellows, Chief Technicians, Senior Technicians, Researchers, Research Assistants, Technicians and Technical Assistants
in teaching and/or research departments and institutes, who are contractually required to carry out teaching, examination
and administrative duties and to conduct research and innovation.

2. TITLE AND DATE OF COMMENCEMENT8
This Ordinance is cited as the Academic Staff Appointments, Grading, Tenure and Promotions Ordinance Number 3 of
2000 as amended and shall take effect from 1 February 2024.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 87]
3. OBJECTIVES
In making this Ordinance, Council seeks to:
3.1 Promote Academic Staff whose performance demonstrates particular merit in teaching, consultancy, student
supervision, research, innovation, enterprise development,

scholarship and creative activity, administration, service and leadership in the University and professional practice
including service to the community.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 87]
3.1.1 Research and Scholarship imply basic, and applied multi-disciplinary research.
3.1.2 Innovation implies the invention, creation and implementation of new processes, products, services and
methods of delivery which result in significant improvements in outcomes, efficiency, effectiveness or
quality.
3.1.3 Enterprise development implies an act of investing time and capital to establish, expand or improve
business.
3.1.4 Creative work entails generation of content attuned to innovation and industrialisation.
3.1.5 Leadership entails more than administrative work; it can entail getting people to understand and believe in
the vision and work to achieve set goals.
3.1.6 Service to the Community entails staff voluntary involvement in activities of different dimensions that

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 87]
3.1.6 Service to the Community entails staff voluntary involvement in activities of different dimensions that
assist the community

text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 87]
3.2 Provide an objective, fair and systematic method of assessment in order to ensure a consistent application of
standards for the appointments and promotions of staff.

on Department or Faculty establishment may be filled up to professorial level.

5. GRADING AND INITIAL APPOINTMENT OF ACADEMIC STAFF

a. On initial appointment to the University's Academic Staff, a successful candidate shall be graded according to his
or her qualifications, experience, published research, proven innovations and industrialisation.

b. Qualifications

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 88]
b. Qualifications

i. The basic qualification for appointment to the University's academic staff at lecturer/research fellow
grade is normally a PhD degree but at least a credit in a Master's degree may be considered in the
critical shortage areas as approved by Senate. This is subject to review from time to time.
ii. The basic qualification for appointment at Teaching Assistants/Research Assistants/Staff Development
Fellow grade is a good Honours Degree in the relevant field. Senate may review this from time to time.
iii. The basic qualification for appointment at Technician grade is a professional diploma and a degree in
the relevant field.
iv. The basic qualification for an appointment at Technical Assistant grade is a professional diploma.

c. Experience

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 88]
c. Experience

i. In granting recognition to relevant postgraduate experience, the University shall:
5.3.3.1 Make no distinction between professional and non-professional experience.
5.3.3.2 Recognise in full, the time spent as a full-time member of the academic (teaching and /or research) staff
of a reputable university/institute.
5.3.3.3 In all disciplines, any postgraduate experience in the appropriate discipline shall be recognized as
relevant.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 88]
5.4 Research, Innovation and Industrialization Output
5.4.1 The University recognises published research in journals, including books and book chapters,
filed/registered Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), innovation, creative work and enterprise development
for the purposes of determining the grade on initial appointment.
5.4.2 The Appointment Board shall take cognisance of the quality of the Research, Innovation, and
Industrialization and decide whether it meets the conditions set by ZIMCHE.
5.4.3 The Appointment Board shall ensure that the assessment and weighting of published research and
filed/registered IPR, creative work, innovation and enterprise development are consistent with standards
implemented by the Promotions Committee (Refer to Annexure 1).

text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 88]
6. GRADING AND SALARY STRUCTURE
a. There shall be only one Academic (Teaching and Research) Grading and Salary Structure, and the same salary
scale shall apply to all posts in all Faculties and Institutes within the University.

7. PROMOTION

a. For one to be promoted, he/she has to be a permanent/full-time member of staff or have a long-term contract of
two or more years that has been renewed more than once.

b. Normally, the basic qualification for promotion is a PhD degree from Lecturer/Research Fellow grades up to
Professor/Research Professor grades; BSc/BA and professional diploma for Technical Assistant, and Master's
degree or a professional diploma from Researcher Technicians upwards.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 88]
c. Conditions for promotion
i. Annual performance reviews shall be considered as part of the promotion requirements.
ii. No member of staff at the level of lecturer /Research Fellow/ Researcher / Chief Technician /Senior
Technician/Technician shall be promoted while on probation.
iii. No member of staff shall be promoted while on full-time study leave.

iv. Criteria for Promotion
In assessing the suitability of members of the academic staff for promotion to a higher grade, the
University shall take into account the following broad criteria.

text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 89]

7.5.1 Assessment of Research
Research is a necessary component in academic life. Those who successfully conduct research geared
at solving the problems of the world deserve credit. No one can be accepted as an academic without
involvement in research.

In assessing a candidate's research, scholarship and creative work (hereinafter referred to as
"research"), the University recognizes that research relates to origination of new knowledge that
advances and/or promotes a discipline and/or its relevance to scholarship and society. It has several
dimensions, and therefore assessment of the candidate's research shall include any of the following
dimensions:

7.10 Composition of the Annual Performance Report

7.10.1 The Annual Performance Report placed in each academic member of staff's personal file each year by
the Head/Chairperson of the Department shall include an assessment of the member's teaching, research,
innovations and industrialization as stipulated in items 7.4 and 7.5. The annual report shall have an
additional section for innovation, consultancy, creative work and enterprise development.

7.10.2 Report on Teaching/Consultancy
In compiling the Section of the Annual Performance Report on a member's teaching the
Head/Chairperson of the Department shall include an evaluation arrived at after implementing at least
the following means of assessment:

7.10.2.1 Peer Evaluation of Teaching/Consultancy

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 95]
The Departmental Board shall establish a panel of at least two academic members of the Department,
with the responsibility of attending lectures/observing consultancy work of their colleagues on different
occasions

and without prior notice to the person giving the lecture/doing consultancy work. The panel's report
shall be considered by the Departmental Board and, after constructive, open discussion with the member
of staff concerned, shall become a component in the assessment of each member of staff's
teaching/consultancy. The evaluation of teaching/consultancy shall also focus on innovation, creative
work and enterprise development.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 95]
7.10.2.2 Evaluation by Students
Students will be provided with an opportunity to complete an evaluation form in respect of each course.
In the first instance, evaluation forms completed by students shall be submitted to the Chairperson of
Department who shall discuss the views expressed with the member of staff concerned and the
Departmental Board before including any formal comment in the Annual Performance Report.

7.10.2.3 Assessment by External Examiners
Any comments by External Examiners on a member's teaching shall be included in the Annual
Performance Report.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:

7.10.2.4 Seminars
All Departments are required to encourage members of staff to hold seminars on relevant subjects of
their choice to which staff and students should be invited to attend. Assessment of presentations in
seminars and public lectures may become part of the evaluation of the members of staff's application
for promotion.

7.10.2.5 Report on Research, Innovation, Creative Work and Enterprise Development
The section of the Annual Performance Report on a member's research shall comprise:
A report prepared by the member of staff, on his/her peer reviewed publications, innovation, creative
work, filing or registration of IPR; enterprise development; conference papers, conference talks and the
status of his/her work in progress during that year.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf

7.10.2.6 Report on Service to the University and Community
The section of the Annual Performance Report on a member's University service shall comprise:

7.10.2.6.1 A report by the Chairperson/ Head of Department/Unit on the member's University service
during the year in question;
7.10.2.6.2 Any written comments by the member's Chairperson/Head of Department/Unit report made
in terms of Section 7.10.1 above.

8. TENURE

8.1 Only citizens and permanent residents of Zimbabwe, in accordance with Section 6 (2) of the University Act
shall be appointed on permanent/full-time terms of service, which permit the granting of tenure in terms of this
Ordinance, should the University so determine.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 96]
8.2 Persons who are not citizens or residents of Zimbabwe shall be appointed only on fixed-term contracts. In the
event that they have completed one contract term successfully, such members shall be entitled to being
considered for tenure, and therefore, further provisions of this section of the Ordinance do apply to such staff.

8.3 All academic staff appointed by the University shall be required to serve a probationary period before being
considered for tenure provided that Appointment Boards, may, where it appears that the candidate so merits it,
decide that a candidate be appointed at the level of Associate Professor/Associate Research Professor or
Professor/Research Professor with immediate tenure.

institution of higher education, tenure maybe transferrable for those academic staff appointed from
similar or recognizable institutions.

8.4.2 In the case of staff who had not previously had tenure: three (3) years.

8.4.3 Technicians: one (1) year

may either:

may either:

8.7.1 Extend the probationary period by up to two further years with permission for the member of staff to
apply for tenure before the expiry of that time; or terminate the member of staff's employment with
the University.

member of staff to apply for tenure before the expiry of that time; or terminate the member of staff's
employment with the University.

text:

8.8 If at the end of the probationary period a member of staff is granted tenure, then the appointment shall be
without time limit up to the age fixed by the University for retirement except that:

8.8.1 A member may resign his/her appointment by giving not less than six months' notice in writing.
8.8.2 For Technicians/Researchers a member may resign his/her appointment by giving not less than three
months' notice in writing.

8.8.3 If a member fails to serve the required notice period, he/she shall be liable to pay the University an
amount equivalent to his/her gross salary for the period not served.

8.8.4 A member may not resign while he/she is on Sabbatical Leave or on Contact Visit.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:

8.8.5 A member who resigns while he/she is on Sabbatical Leave or on Contact Visit shall be required to
repay the University Sabbatical airfares received, salary received whilst on Sabbatical or Contact Visit,
University contributions to member's pension scheme and six months' salary in lieu of notice.

8.8.6 Any period preceding or spent on such leave or visit shall not be counted as a period or portion of a
period of notice.

8.8.7 The University Council may terminate the appointment for "good cause" by giving the member of staff
not less than six months' notice or paying the member's salary in lieu thereof. This should be done in
accordance with the University Code of Conduct.

1. INTERPRETATION
The University Officers charged with the administration of these rules will at all times seek to implement the letter
and spirit of the University Act and will in particular have regard to the following principles:-
1.1 the University is a society in which high standards of communal life must be established and maintained
for the benefit of both present and future members of the University.
1.2 a high level of personal integrity and a development sense of responsibility towards others are as important
to the University as outstanding scholastic achievement.
1.3 a proper concern for the reputation of the University and what it ought to stand for
makes it incumbent upon its members to live decent and ordered lives.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 104]
makes it incumbent upon its members to live decent and ordered lives.
1.4 individual or collective action by members of the University which constitutes a breach of these rules
may require to be punished notwithstanding that the motive or goal of such action was commendable in
the belief of such members.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 105]
2. UNDERTAKING AT REGISTRATION
When registering as a member of the University a student shall be given a copy of these rules and shall sign a
statement in which he/she acknowledges that he/she has been furnished with the rules, and he/she undertakes to
conduct himself/herself while a student of the University in accordance therewith and with any amendments duly
made thereto.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 105]
3. STUDENT CONDUCT
3.1 No student of the University shall:
3.1.1 use the University premises contrary to University Regulations, Residence, Faculty or
Departmental rules or do any act reasonably likely to cause such misuse.
3.1.2 damage or deface any property of the University or do any act reasonably
likely to cause damage or defacement thereto.
3.1.3 disrupt teaching, study, research or administrative work, or prevent any member of the University
or its staff from carrying on his/her study or work, or do any act reasonably likely to cause disruption
or prevention and
3.1.4 engage in any conduct whether on or off the campus which is or is reasonably likely to be harmful to
the interests of the University, members of the University staff or students.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 105]
3.2 The following would be regarded by the University as stances of breaches of the rule contained in
3.1 above:
3.2.1 displaying violence by word or act towards any member of the University, whether academic or
administrative staff or student, or a guest of the University, or any visitor to the University or in
any way intimidating or obstructing the free movement of such a member, guest or visitor.
3.2.2 disrupting or seeking to disrupt any proper function of the University whether it be an official
function, Council meeting, Senate meeting, Faculty or Committee meeting, lecture, teaching
session, the function of any University Society or day-today administrative activity.
3.2.3 Seeking to prevent a speaker invited by any section of this University Community

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 105]
3.2.3 Seeking to prevent a speaker invited by any section of this University Community
from lawfully expressing his/her views.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 105]
3.3 Students are informed that:-
3.3.1 if a group of students form a common intention to commit certain acts and to assist each other in their
commission, and in due course a breach of these rules is committed by one or some of the group,
then each member of the group may be held to have committed that breach of the rules, who foresaw
that the breach would occur, or who must, in the view of the Student Disciplinary Committee, have
foreseen that it would occur. A member of such a group can avoid this happening to him/her by
taking clear and unequivocal steps, before such a breach is committed, to show that he/she
dissociates himself from the acts of the group with whom he/she has so far been associating.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 105]
dissociates himself from the acts of the group with whom he/she has so far been associating.
3.3.2 Where a number of students have committed a breach of these rules and only one or more of these
students can be identified, the University will not hesitate to take disciplinary action against those
students who can be identified and against whom there is sufficient evidence to warrant
investigation.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 106]
3.3.3 Where a student commits an act which is both an offence according to the laws of the country and
one which after investigation appears to be a breach of the disciplinary rules of the University, the
University may punish such a student notwithstanding that he/she is prosecuted and/or punished
by the courts of the country.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 106]
3.4 A student shall obey any rules made from time to time by the Vice-Chancellor and shall further obey all
instructions given by the Vice-Chancellor, the Proctors, and all those persons whom the Vice-Chancellor
has charged to assist him in the maintenance of discipline, and in this regard:-
3.4.1 any Executive Dean, Deputy Dean, Chairperson of Department, Librarian, Deputy Librarian or
member of the senior administrative staff may order any member of a gathering of students which
is committing, or whose activities are likely to lead to a breach of Rule 3 above, to disperse, and
may further order any such member to furnish his/her full name or accompany the member of staff for
an interview with the Vice-Chancellor or a Proctor, or give both such orders. For the purpose of

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf

this section, Senior Administrative Staff shall include the Registrar, the Deputy Registrar

Dean of Students, Deputy Dean of Students, Assistant to the Vice-Chancellor, and Wardens of Halls

3.4.2 if a student misbehaves in a lecture or teaching session or interferes with the conduct of a lecture

6. RULES FOR HALLS OF RESIDENCE

6.1 General
A resident shall obey all rules made and instructions given by the Warden, Deputy and Sub Warden of the
residence and shall refrain from conduct which:
6.1.1 may bring discredit upon his/her hall of residence or
6.1.2 is prejudicial to the welfare of other residents of the hall.

6.2 Powers of Hall Committee Members
Members of a Hall Committee shall have the power, to investigate, and if necessary reprimand residents
for any infringements of the rules contained in this section, and report such investigation or reprimand to
the Warden.

A resident shall be liable to compensate the University in full for any damage caused by him/her to
University property. Damage caused to a study - bedroom shall be presumed to have been caused by the
resident to whom such a room has been allocated unless the contrary is proved.

6.4 Fire
A resident having knowledge of the outbreak of fire in, or adjacent to Hall premises
shall as soon as possible:
6.4.1 inform the Warden, Deputy or Sub-Warden
6.4.2 summon the Municipal Fire-Brigade
6.4.3 inform the Director of Works and Estates.

prescribed channels and on the prescribed form.
6.5.3 a resident granted leave to reside in a Hall of residence during vacation who no longer wishes to
avail himself/herself of this privilege shall furnish the Executive Dean of Students with at least 3

penalty.

to that of the Warden. A resident of a Hall may be required to be in the Hall every night by such time as
may be laid down in Regulations unless prior permission has been granted by the Warden or Sub-Warden

text:

1. PREAMBLE
In terms of section 29 (3) (h) of the University Act No.4 of 1999, the Council of the Midlands State University, with the
approval of the Minister of Higher and Tertiary Education, Innovation, Science and Technology Development, or such
other Minister to whom the President may from time to time assign the administration of the Midlands State University Act
on the recommendation of the University Senate, makes the following Ordinance:
2. TITLE
This ordinance may be cited as the Innovation and Industrialisation Ordinance Number 8 of 2023.
3. INTERPRETATION
In this Ordinance:
3.1. Commercialisation shall refer to the transfer of intellectual property to bring or to create new products or services

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 113]
In this Ordinance:
3.1. Commercialisation shall refer to the transfer of intellectual property to bring or to create new products or services
to the market; create awareness, establish distribution channels, and promote the trial and purchase of the goods
and services.
3.2. Community innovators shall refer to innovators who are outside the university and are from the community.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 114]
3.3. Contracted research shall refer to legally bound research between the University and external partners. This
research is conducted under agreed terms and conditions such as inter alia funding and ownership of research
outputs.
3.4. Enterprise shall refer to any profitable commercial venture.
3.5. Heritage-Based Education 5.0 shall refer to an education system that includes teaching, research, community
service, innovation, and industrialisation with a heritage-based philosophy that emphasises industrialisation
through innovation and knowledge of Zimbabwe's natural resources.
3.6. Industrialisation shall refer to the setting up of industries and processes that shall translate innovations and
research outputs into goods and services.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 114]
research outputs into goods and services.
3.7. Innovation shall refer to using relevant knowledge and resources to convert ideas into new products, processes, or
practices or improve the existing product(s), process, or practice.
3.8. Innovator shall refer to an individual, company, or group of individuals who create new methods, ideas, or
products.
3.9. Intellectual Property (IP) shall refer to mental creations such as inventions, literary and artistic works, designs
and commercial symbols, names, and images. Patents, trademarks, trade secrets, utility models, industrial designs,
and copyright laws can all protect intellectual property in various forms.
3.10. Invention means the act of putting ideas or objects together in a unique and novel way to create something that did

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 114]
3.10. Invention means the act of putting ideas or objects together in a unique and novel way to create something that did
not exist before.
3.11. Spin-out refers to any venture that springs out of knowledge capital created by any of the University's internal
stakeholders. It can be a start-up, spin-off, or joint venture.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 114]
3.11.1. Joint Venture shall mean a commercial arrangement between two or
more participants who agree to do business together wherein the parties create an entity by contributing equity and
share the revenues, expenses, and control of the enterprise in proportion to their capital contribution, e.g., Special
Purpose Vehicle (SPV)

3.11.2. Special Purpose Vehicle shall refer to a company, which comprises the
university and other shareholders, registered with a specific mandate to undertake a specific project of commercial
interest.
3.11.3. Spin-off company shall mean a business created by the University
whose technology is owned by the University, financed by the University, and managed by the University.
3.11.4. Start-up company shall mean a business in the first stages of operations.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 114]
3.12. Technology shall refer to the application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes.
3.13. Technology transfer (TT) shall be defined as the transfer of new technologies, inventions/creations, and
discoveries from university/research institutions to parties capable of commercialization for the framework.
3.14. University shall mean Midlands State University.
3.15. University Company shall mean a company wholly owned by the University.

4. APPLICATION

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 115]
This ordinance applies to all innovators including University students and staff members, Faculties, Institutes, Centres
as well as the community.

text:

5. OBJECTIVES
In making this Ordinance, Council seeks to:
5.1 Promote a culture of research, innovation, and industrialisation within the University and beyond by supporting
innovative initiatives by University staff members, students, and the community.
5.2 Provide for the commercialisation of university intellectual property into commercial industrial ventures or enterprises.
5.3 Enable the conversion of innovations and inventions from university and community research and development outputs
into goods and services.
5.4 Foster collaboration with the community, industry, and commerce thus enabling technology development and transfer.
5.5 Promote the creation and sustainable growth of Start-ups, Spin-offs, Spin-off companies, and Special Purpose
Vehicles.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 115]
5.5 Promote the creation and sustainable growth of Start-ups, Spin-offs, Spin-off companies, and Special Purpose
Vehicles.
5.6 Protect intellectual property by providing adequate legal protection against unauthorized use.
5.7 Create a framework for promoting and protecting innovators.

d) ensure innovators are promoted and facilitated;
e) stimulate and manage the flow of knowledge and technology across innovators and markets; and
f) facilitate application for intellectual property rights
g) facilitate the acquisition of relevant technology

9.1. On joining the University, each employee shall enter into a three (3) months probationary period. During this period,

a) production of prioritised goods and services arising from prototypes, industrial designs, or other IP rights generated

11.3. Community-based Innovators: This stream draws on innovations generated by individuals engaged in diverse

12.2. The Technical Committee shall evaluate MSU's research products/services/technologies/IP/IPR before
commercialisation. They shall preside over disputed areas in the selection, protection, and commercialization of

13. THE INCUBATION PROCESS
13.1. The Incubation process shall be as follows:
13.1.1. Predisclosure of innovation/invention/creation
13.1.2. Full disclosure of innovation/invention/creation
13.1.3. Assessment of innovation/invention/creation
13.1.4. Signing of Incubation agreement and non-disclosure agreements.
13.1.5. IP protection, filing, and enforcement.

16. MANAGEMENT OF INNOVATION OUTPUTS AND IPRs
16.1. The University innovation outputs and IPRs shall be governed following the University IP Policy, Spin-out Policy,
and Commercialisation Policy.
16.2. The Principal Investigator (PI) or lead innovator shall be regarded as the originator of the original idea and strategic
leader of the innovation process. There shall be only one PI to an Innovation Project or Programme

original idea, providing strategic leadership support to the research/innovation process. There may be more than
one Co-PI to a project or programme.
16.4. The PI, Co-PI, and any other persons who have contributed significantly to the innovation shall be regarded
collectively as innovators.
16.5. A Start-up company, where the Innovator(s) shall get at least 70% of the net income and the University gets up to
30% of the net income in the first 5 (five) years, and then innovators shall get 90% and the University 10% in the

17. GOVERNANCE AND SHARE OWNERSHIP STRUCTURE OF COMPANIES
17.1. The Governance and share ownership structure of companies shall be as follows:
17.1.1. Category A: Start-up Companies
a) Directorship: The Principal Innovator and Co-Innovators shall be among the principal directors or appoint their
representatives on the Start-up Company Board, while the University shall appoint a Director(s) to the Board to
represent its interests.
b) Shareholding: The Principal Innovator and Co-Innovators shall have a majority shareholding in any Start-up, with

and expert support.
c) The Start-up company shares shall not be sold without the written consent of the University.

GENERAL ACADEMIC REGULATIONS FOR UNDERGRADUATE C E R T I F I C A T E S A N D
DIPLOMAS OF THE MIDLANDS STATE UNIVERSITY

1. PREAMBLE

1.1 Senate shall be the final authority for the interpretation of these Regulations.
1.2 Senate has the power to exempt any student from any of the regulations.
1.3 A student who has started a programme following one set of regulations will not be affected by
regulations subsequently adopted unless agreed to in writing by the student.
1.4 Every student, by the act of registering with a Faculty, agrees to abide by all the rules, regulations and policies
of the University, the Faculty, and the relevant Department.
1.5 In these Regulations the following terms shall be used as described:-

Programme: a plan of study lasting a period of time, which leads to the award of a
diploma or degree of the University.

a defined portion of a programme.

a field of study offered by a Department.

a separately examinable component within a subject.

2.1 The Diplomas offered by the University are carried out primarily through taught modules with continuous
assessment and examinations offered at the end of a semester.
2.2 Studies may be pursued on a full-time or part-time basis as prescribed by Faculties in
their Regulations.

3. FACULTY REGULATIONS

3.1 There shall be Faculty Regulations for Diploma studies, which shall be read in conjunction with the General
Academic Regulations. Specific restrictions on the choice of subjects, modules and additional requirements
may be specified in the Departmental Regulations.

Holders of at least a certificate or at least five 'O' Level Passes including English.
5.2 Mature Entry
The Faculty or Department may use their discretion on maturity entry.

A prescribed period of hands-on practical experience in a relevant industrial, commercial /

8. INTERRUPTION OF STUDY

8.1 A student who breaks his or her studies for more than two consecutive semesters without the approval of
the Senate shall normally be deemed to have lost any accumulated credits. Such a student may be allowed
to re-apply for admission to the University
8.2 A student who wishes to interrupt his or her study programme shall apply in advance to the Faculty through
the Head of Department and Deans of the appropriate Faculty, stating reasons why he/she wants to interrupt
his/her study programme. Permission must duly be granted before he/she leaves the University. The
decision of the Senate shall be communicated to the applicant by the Deputy Registrar Academic.

A student who does not fulfil the requirements for any module shall not be allowed to take the examination

11.2 If a student is repeating a module(s) he or she shall only be credited with the marks obtained during the
'repeat' examination.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 123]
12.1 Students must be guided by the University's Anti-plagiarism and Responsible use of Artificial Intelligence
(AI) Policy
12.2 Plagiarism is an academic offence and the University does not tolerate it whatsoever.
12.3 Plagiarism is the unacknowledged use of another person's material or ideas. As such, plagiarism is an academic
offence in the sense that theft is in ordinary daily life.
12.4 Recommendations on the severity of the penalty shall be determined by the appropriate Departmental Board
or Panel of Examiners. Cases of plagiarism shall be handled in the following manner: -
12.5 Minor Cases of Plagiarism
• First Offence: in the case of plagiarism being discovered in a piece of work such as an essay

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 123]
12.5 Minor Cases of Plagiarism
• First Offence: in the case of plagiarism being discovered in a piece of work such as an essay
or laboratory report or dissertation the student shall get a Chairperson's warning but shall be
given an opportunity to re-do and re-submit an acceptable piece of work after one week and
shall be awarded a maximum mark of 50%.
• Second Offence: The student shall get a Dean's warning and shall be awarded a mark of
zero.
• Third Offence: Senate shall take disciplinary measures such as suspension or expulsion of
the student who will have been awarded a mark of zero.
12.6 Major Cases of Plagiarism
• In the case of plagiarism being discovered in a project at end of the semester, that candidate
shall be denied the opportunity to resubmit the project.

file_name: HUMANITIES -GENERAL INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS final done (1).pdf
text:
[MSU Humanities Yearbook, p. 123]
shall be denied the opportunity to resubmit the project.
15.5.1.1 The new project shall be submitted in the second semester after the discovery of the
offence.
15.5.1.2 The new project shall be awarded a maximum mark of 50%.
• In the case of plagiarism being discovered in a project for the second time and after re-
submission, a mark of zero shall be awarded and recorded, and Senate shall take disciplinary
action either to suspend or expel the student.

2. PROGRAMMES
2.1 The University may offer programmes for undergraduate Bachelor's Degrees at General
and Honours levels.
